bug_description: A CHECK failure (assertion abort) occurs in DiagnosePoisonedName() (toolchain/check/name_lookup.cpp:703) in the Carbon language compiler when a function `fn Name()` is defined in Carbon code after an inline C++ import block defines a class `Carbon::Name`. The name lookup system marks 'Name' as poisoned (state = Poisoned) because the inline C++ import introduces it into the Carbon namespace, but fails to record the poisoning source location. When BuildFunctionDecl() (handle_function.cpp:194) detects the poisoned state and calls DiagnosePoisonedName(), the CARBON_CHECK assertion `poisoning_loc_id.has_value()` fires because no location was stored, causing the compiler to abort with SIGABRT (exit code 134).
build_sh:
#!/bin/bash -eu
set -eu
cd /src/carbon-lang

# Rebuild carbon-busybox binary after patching.
# Bazel cache from Docker build makes this an incremental rebuild.
bazel build -c opt //toolchain/install:carbon-busybox 2>&1

if [ ! -f bazel-bin/toolchain/install/carbon-busybox ]; then
    echo "ERROR: carbon-busybox binary not found after build"
    exit 1
fi

echo "Carbon binary built successfully"
secb_sh:
#!/bin/bash

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/carbon-lang
    if bazel build -c opt //toolchain/install:carbon-busybox 2>&1; then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    echo "REPRODUCING THE ISSUE FOR carbon-lang.issue-7162..."
    /src/carbon-lang/bazel-bin/toolchain/install/carbon-busybox compile \
        --output=/tmp/output.s --asm-output /testcase/poc.carbon 2>&1
    # NOTE: YOU SHOULD NOT RETURN/EXIT 0 IN THIS FUNCTION.
    # The binary will abort (exit 134) on the CHECK failure.
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/carbon-lang
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"

    case "$command" in
        build)
            build "$@"
            ;;
        repro)
            repro "$@"
            ;;
        patch)
            patch "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi
dockerfile:
FROM ubuntu:22.04
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ENV SRC=/src
ENV FUZZING_LANGUAGE=cpp
ENV SANITIZER=none
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    git curl wget ca-certificates python3 python3-pip build-essential \
    zip unzip xz-utils file libxml2 libncurses5 libedit2 zlib1g \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
RUN cd /tmp && \
    wget -q "https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/releases/download/llvmorg-19.1.7/LLVM-19.1.7-Linux-X64.tar.xz" && \
    mkdir -p /opt/llvm && \
    tar -xJf LLVM-19.1.7-Linux-X64.tar.xz --strip-components=1 -C /opt/llvm && \
    rm LLVM-19.1.7-Linux-X64.tar.xz && \
    rm -f /opt/llvm/lib/*.a && \
    rm -f /opt/llvm/bin/{flang-*,mlir-*,clang-{scan-deps,check,repl},*-test,llvm-{lto*,reduce,bolt*,exegesis,jitlink},bugpoint}
ENV PATH="/opt/llvm/bin:${PATH}"
RUN wget -q -O /usr/local/bin/bazelisk \
    "https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazelisk/releases/download/v1.25.0/bazelisk-linux-amd64" && \
    chmod +x /usr/local/bin/bazelisk && \
    ln -s /usr/local/bin/bazelisk /usr/local/bin/bazel
RUN mkdir -p $SRC && cd $SRC && \
    git init carbon-lang && cd carbon-lang && \
    git remote add origin https://github.com/carbon-language/carbon-lang.git && \
    git fetch --depth=1 origin 62b94f79322039acc3fc8e175896a64a32df470e && \
    git checkout FETCH_HEAD && \
    rm -rf .git && git init && \
    git config user.email "secbench@local" && \
    git config user.name "secbench" && \
    git add -A && git commit -m "carbon-lang at 62b94f7 (pre-patch)"
WORKDIR $SRC/carbon-lang
RUN printf 'build --disk_cache=\nbuild --jobs=HOST_CPUS*.75\nbuild --verbose_failures\n' > user.bazelrc
RUN bazel build -c opt //toolchain/install:carbon-busybox
RUN printf '#!/bin/bash\ncd /src/carbon-lang && bazel build -c opt //toolchain/install:carbon-busybox 2>&1\n' \
    > /usr/local/bin/compile && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/compile
RUN mkdir -p /testcase
COPY poc.carbon /testcase/poc.carbon
COPY build.sh $SRC/
COPY secb.sh /usr/local/bin/secb
RUN chmod +x /usr/local/bin/secb

bug_report:
================= Bug Report (1/1) ==================
## Source: GitHub Issue
## URL: https://github.com/carbon-language/carbon-lang/issues/7162
## Description:
Issue: carbon-language/carbon-lang#7162
Title: Carbon crashes when `fn Name` is defined after an inline C++ block defines `Carbon::Name`
State: open
Created at: 2026-05-05

Issue Body:
A CHECK failure (internal assertion abort) occurs in the Carbon compiler when processing a source file that defines a function name that conflicts with a class name introduced via an inline C++ import block in the `Carbon` namespace.

The crash occurs in `DiagnosePoisonedName()` at `toolchain/check/name_lookup.cpp:703`. The name lookup system correctly detects that the name 'Name' is in a 'Poisoned' state (used before its Carbon declaration), but when it attempts to emit a diagnostic, the `poisoning_loc_id` field has no value. This triggers the `CARBON_CHECK(poisoning_loc_id.has_value())` assertion, which calls `abort()` and kills the compiler with SIGABRT (exit code 134).

The root cause is that names imported from inline C++ blocks into the `Carbon` namespace create a poisoned-name entry in the name lookup table without recording a valid source location for the poisoning point. When a subsequent Carbon declaration with the same name triggers the poisoned-name diagnostic path, the missing location causes the assertion failure.

**Crash location:** toolchain/check/name_lookup.cpp:703, function DiagnosePoisonedName()
**Call path:** BuildFunctionDecl() (handle_function.cpp:194) -> DiagnosePoisonedName()

**Reproduction:** Compile the following Carbon source file:
```carbon
import Cpp inline '''c++
namespace Carbon {
  class Name {};
}
''';

fn Name() {}
```

**Vulnerable version:** 0.0.0-0.nightly.2026.05.01+62b94f7 (commit 62b94f79322039acc3fc8e175896a64a32df470e)
